title: Artel bounded native storage protocol v1

after.description: Exclusive fixed-index sort tuple, optionally followed by record id. No-sort indexes require [id]. Mutually exclusive with cursor. Numeric order values are nonnegative safe integers.

quarantine.description: First quarantined reclaim elements. An element that fails three consecutive passes is recorded under m:reclaim-quarantine:<kind>:<element> and the cursor moves on.

hash.input: request body with recursively canonicalized objects; requestId and payloadHash omitted before hashing
hash.numeric: all protocol integers are JSON numbers in [0,9007199254740991] (2^53-1); payload numbers MUST be finite I-JSON values representable by JCS; reject NaN, Infinity and integers outside this bound; Rust and JS MUST use the same JCS implementation

idempotency.same_hash: return original receipt exactly (including durable/outcome state)
idempotency.timeout_after_admission: outcome_unknown; write continues; resolve by receipt; never auto-retry under a new operationId

sequence.entries: span=max(1,entries.length); metadata-only writes consume one operation tick, no synthetic native entry

dependencySemantics.writeAndBarrier: wait only for own prefix and listed dependency prefixes; never global drain or future operations

durability.buffered: WAL enabled, admission/applied may precede physical sync
durability.required: physical WAL sync before durable receipt

errors.outcome_unknown: admitted operation may commit; query receipt
errors.stale_incarnation: ticket belongs to prior runtime incarnation
errors.storage_error: RocksDB I/O or corruption only; the owner becomes degraded
errors.invalid_cursor: cursor was not issued for this read scope/kind/cut/leaf or names a position outside it; request error, storage stays ready
errors.retryable: transient read/admission condition (deadline, concurrent reclaim of a deleted generation); nothing changed, retry
errors.rejected_before_apply: conflict/schema validation after admission is durably receipted (outcome conflict, not_applied); receipt lookup never returns outcome_unknown for it

bodyLedger.layout: <data>/blobs/.managed: live/<hash> is the only body (sidecars <hash>.png|jpg|gif|webp|svg are hardlinks), intents/<hash>/<pid>.<startMs>.<uuid>[.abandoned], staging/<uuid>.tmp, locks/<hash>.lock, gc.lock (backup pin). Everything else under the root is ignored.
bodyLedger.publication: Producer: intent, stage or reuse, link under locks/<hash>.lock, durable owner write, delete intent; on failure rename the intent to .abandoned. An intent of a live producer (pid alive, start within 5 s) pins its hash; a dead or abandoned one is retired with its staging file.

keys.O: O<ownerKey>: sorted hashes owned by that record
keys.H: H<hash>\0<ownerKey>: owner row, written in the owner's batch
keys.c: c<hash>: deletion candidate (logical C; tag C is the native child index). Set when an owner drops the hash or a retired intent leaves an unowned body
keys.D: D<hash>: delete in progress; an owner write of that hash is a conflict
keys.V: V<hash>: {bytes, children}; the body was hashed once, later references only stat its size
keys.m:reclaim-quarantine: m:reclaim-quarantine:<native|blob>:<sha256 of the native row key | body hash>: {kind, element, phase, error, at}; written after three consecutive failures of that element; native Search skips it, a quarantined body keeps its file and loses c/D/V

bodyLedger.sweep: Per candidate, bounded per pass: no H, lock(hash), no live intent, D under apply_lock, unlink body and sidecars, delete D, c and V.
bodyLedger.uploads: C5: metadata blob-upload:<key> exists only as state=ready with ready_at (ms epoch), is written once and then only deleted; it owns its body. The body reclaim tombstones rows older than ready_at + 7 days through the upload_ready index (bounded per pass); consuming, removing or expiring the row makes its body a candidate unless another owner holds it. An inbox acceptance whose upload row is gone is conflict 'ready upload descriptor missing'.

stateTransitions.durability: applied -> durable only after required WAL sync; buffered may remain applied
stateTransitions.disconnect: admitted_pending|applied|durable remains owned; caller sees outcome_unknown until receipt lookup
stateTransitions.stale: any nonterminal old-incarnation ticket -> stale_incarnation; never durable

numericContract.seqEncoding: JSON integer, never decimal float/exponent; reject >2^53-1
numericContract.rustJs: Rust serde and JS JCS serializers must agree; add golden vectors for integer, 1.0, exponent, unicode-key and nested payload cases

readSemantics.cursor: Opaque versioned string binds kind, family/generation, frozen cut, selected context leaf and next traversal position; cross-scope/kind/cut/leaf reuse or a forged position is invalid_cursor. No retained snapshot.
readSemantics.watermarks: durableThroughSeq is required WAL prefix; liveThroughSeq is applied prefix; no read waits for future writes
readSemantics.empty: Empty generation is valid: barrier/read response throughSeq=durableThroughSeq=liveThroughSeq=0 and events=[]; concrete response schemas allow minimum=0.
readSemantics.context: Newest-to-oldest selected leaf ancestry only; seq is origin-generation-local, entryId is family-unique. Bounded snapshot, decoded bytes, serialized full response bytes and traversal steps; oversize first record and corrupt records are explicit errors.
readSemantics.decodedBudget: A read page also bounds the stored bytes it decodes (maxBytes + one maximal event). Reaching that bound ends the page deterministically with a cursor at the next entry (skipped removed or replaced entries may make it short or empty); a first record larger than maxBytes is schema_error.

generationSemantics.initial: generation starts at firstSeq=1; first write with firstSeq!=1 is sequence_gap
generationSemantics.continuity: Admission firstSeq=highest reserved contiguous prefix+1, initially appliedThroughSeq+1; execution follows applied predecessor. Duplicates checked before reservation.
generationSemantics.gap: sequence_gap before admission; no receipt mutation
generationSemantics.lineage: Immutable parent generation/cut/leaf; first write explicitly depends on parent cut unless zero. No ancestor body copies. Head leaf defaults to final new entry; explicit null means before first entry.

fencing.request: write/barrier/read/receipt carry incarnation; mismatch returns stale_incarnation before admission
fencing.response: Envelope echoes current incarnation; embedded receipt preserves original generation and incarnation. Stale write rejected before duplicate lookup. Current-fence rehash conflicts with original receipt.

hashProjection.canonicalInput: Complete write object after removing only requestId and payloadHash. Includes incarnation. Optional absence is preserved; null object fields rejected. RFC8785 JCS, with all integral payload values outside +/- (2^53-1) rejected.
goldenVectors: same body different requestId => same hash
unicode keys use JCS UTF-16 order

x-artel.responseEnvelope: Success OR common errorResponse; authenticated malformed request may use requestId=null. Unauthorized is transport HTTP401 before protocol.
x-artel.receiptIdentity: Family+operationId unique; request generation must match original receipt. Duplicate returns authoritative current state, no second enqueue. Missing receipt is outcome_unknown.
x-artel.transport: POST write/barrier/read/receipt/runtime_query/backup accepts canonical envelope; route must match operation. GET health/metrics/reclaim_status are bodyless. Every route has its own body limit (routes.maxBodyBytes). Before parsing, unauthorized401, unknown route404, admission429, body over the route limit413 and deadline408 are transport-only empty responses; no fabricated requestId or protocol receipt.
x-artel.runtime: Finite typed CAS records, fixed derived indexes; every changed key has one expected revision check. Tombstones retain revision. Index cursor binds partition revision; changed partition returns conflict. Full response bounded records+bytes.
x-artel.conditional: runtime or expectedThroughSeq requires idle own scope; successors and dependencies on its pending reservation rejected with backpressure. Known CAS/schema rejection is durably receipted without head advance and never degrades storage. No barrier/dependency may use a not_applied receipt.
x-artel.nativeEdits: Addressed replacement/tombstone at operation cut with expectedThroughSeq; original locator stable, old/fork cuts preserved. Tombstone cannot orphan effective children. read_children pages reverse-parent candidates and may return empty progressing pages.
x-artel.nativeContext: head/state frozen at cut; absent write head/state preserves prior effective values. startEntryId inclusive, current default head anchor only; explicit alternate leaf ignores default checkpoint. No OMP semantics in Rust.
x-artel.runtimeIndexSemantics: Fixed field-derived catalog. Index cursor binds incarnation/partition/revision; any partition mutation invalidates it. after restarts from an exclusive typed keyset lower bound against the current short snapshot. Runtime record revisions persist through tombstones. Resolved inputs are excluded from projection_target/projection_attempt. event_projection tuple is [channel,scope,attempt,kind]. inbox_agent_pending partitions by [agent_instance_id], contains only inbox subtype=item with disposition=pending, and orders by numeric position then id; inbox_agent retains all dispositions. upload_ready has no partition, contains every metadata subtype=blob_upload row and orders by ready_at then id.
x-artel.runtimeSortTypes: All ordered scalar fields are safe unsigned integers except session.updated_at (ISO string); inbox.deliver_at may be null (sorts before numeric timestamps). after follows declared sort fields with optional final id; after without id excludes all records equal to that sort tuple. event_lifecycle is descending by positive event_id; after uses its original positive value.
